accepted.question_text: Consider a bilinear quantum control system (A, B) on a separable Hilbert space H that is k-weakly-coupled for every k > 0, and let (φ_j)_{j\in\mathbb{N}} be a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors of the skew-adjoint drift operator A. Starting from the first eigenstate φ_1, explicitly identify a target state ψ_b \in H that is not colinear to φ_1 and for which there exist a control u \in L^1(\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{R}) and a time T > 0 such that the propagator of the controlled system satisfies Υ^u_{T,0}φ_1 = ψ_b.
accepted.context_brief: Reachable state beyond the first eigenstate

evidence.quote: Question 1: Let (A, B) be k-weakly-coupled for every k > 0. Give (explicitly) a state ψb not colinear to φ1 such that there exist a control u in L1(R, R) and a time T > 0 for which ΥuT,0φ1 = ψb.
Most of the bilinear quantum systems we encountered in the physics literature are k-weakly-coupled for every k > 0.

accepted.question_text: Let (A, B) be a bilinear quantum control system satisfying Assumption 1, with A unbounded, B having no eigenvector, and (A, B) k-weakly-coupled for every k > 0. Assume (A, B) admits a non-degenerate chain of connectedness, so that the union of states reachable from the first eigenstate φ_1 is dense in H, and define ρ as the infimum of times T \ge 0 such that the set of states reachable from φ_1 by piecewise constant controls during times 0 \le t \le T is all of H. Does there exist such a system for which this minimal time parameter satisfies ρ > 0?
accepted.context_brief: Positive minimal time for weakly-coupled systems

evidence.quote: Let (A, B) satisfy Assumption 1 and admit a non-degenerate chain of connectedness. From Proposition 5, we know that ∪t≥0{Υut,0φ1|u ∈ P C} is dense in H. We define ρ = inf {T ≥ 0 such that ∪0≤t≤T {Υut,0φ1|u ∈ P C} = H}.
Question 2: Does it exist (A, B) k-weakly-coupled for every k > 0 such that A is unbounded, B has no eigenvector and ρ > 0?

accepted.question_text: Fix a bilinear quantum control system (A, B) and suppose an upper bound on the L^1 norm of the control is prescribed. Under that L^1-budget constraint, what is the smallest transfer time required to steer the system from the first eigenstate of the drift operator A to the second eigenstate?

evidence.quote: Question 3: An upper bound on the L1 norm of the control being given, what is the smallest possible time needed to transfer a given system (A, B) from the first eigenstate of A to the second one?
As previously said, large controls may, for some examples, allow approximate controllability in arbitrarily small time.

accepted.question_text: Let (A, B) satisfy Assumption 1 and assume it admits a non-degenerate chain of connectedness. Then, for every target state ψ_b on the unit sphere of H and every ε > 0, there exists a piecewise constant control u_ε : [0, T_ε] 	o {0,1} such that the propagated first eigenstate Υ^{u_ε}_{T_ε,0}φ_1 is within ε of ψ_b. Is it possible to choose such controls so that, as ε 	o 0, the number of discontinuities grows strictly slower than 1/ε, that is, is of order o_{ε	o 0}(1/ε)?

evidence.quote: Let (A, B) satisfy Assumption 1. If (A, B) admits a non-degenerate chain of connectedness, then for every ψb in the unit sphere of H, for every ε > 0, there exists uε : [0, Tε] → {0, 1} such that kΥuTu,0φ1 −ψbk < ε. Using [16, Proposition 3], it is possible to build uε with a number of discontinuities of the order of 1/ε.
Question 4: Is it possible to build uε with a number of discontinuities of order oε→0(1/ε)?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a bilinear quantum control system (A, B) in which the control operator B is unbounded, the pair (A, B) satisfies Assumption 1, the system is not k-weakly-coupled for any k > 0, and yet the infinite-dimensional dynamics can still be approximated by its Galerkin truncations uniformly with respect to the L^1 norm of the control?
accepted.context_brief: Uniform Galerkin approximation beyond weak coupling

evidence.quote: Question 5: Does it exist a system (A, B) with unbounded B that satisfies Assumption 1, is not k-weakly-coupled for any k > 0 and that can be approached, uniformly with respect of the L1 norm of the control, by its Galerkin approximations?
The existence of Good Galerkin Approximations is of crucial interest for the theoretical analysis and the numerical simulation of bilinear quantum systems.
